interfaces.name: IsolateData identity
interfaces.contract: Each codec State owns an IsolateData bound to its actual Isolate. Environment returns that stable instance rather than a thread-local facade. Stack initializer adapters bind to the actual current Isolate. Access validates the current native frame owner and foreground thread; copying the native identity is forbidden.
interfaces.limits: Full multi-isolate/worker/fork/retirement conformance is not established by these selected controls.

interfaces.name: IsolateData.options/Environment.options
interfaces.contract: Return shared_ptrs to the original parsed PerIsolateOptions/EnvironmentOptions objects retained by the actual runtime options owner. Native getters select the principal environment context, preserve native record identity/lifetime and observe configuration replacement on subsequent reads. Failed profiles retain the existing pending exception; no default record is manufactured. Owner-local pointer borrowing does not reacquire the process mutex, so native callers may already hold it.
interfaces.limits: Healthy initialized runtime is the normal native caller precondition. Full failed-bootstrap/fatal cleanup remains unvalidated.

interfaces.name: Native process/fatal options and mutex aliases
interfaces.contract: Native process/fatal aliases reference the original parser shared_ptr variable and actual canonical libuv-backed Mutex. Buffer, environment/error consumers read the same original records. The handwritten Buffer/environment/fatal value structures and snapshot accessor are removed.
interfaces.limits: Parsing/storing an option does not implement its behavior. Complete engine/config/security/reporting/permission flag adoption remains unavailable or partial.

interfaces.name: Original option type sharing
interfaces.contract: Whole unchanged node_options.h supplies the same actual classes to both native marshalling adapters. Scoped macro preservation keeps each caller marshalling/assertion owner. Both adapters use the same original canonical Mutex type; no V8 heap or serialization data is used.
